whatItIs.text: A neutral all-purpose oil (usually soybean or canola blend) for frying, baking, and anything where the oil should stay out of the flavour's way.

historyNote.text: The modern bottle is young: Wilhelm Normann hydrogenated liquid fats in 1901, Procter & Gamble launched cottonseed-based Crisco in 1911, and soybean oil ruled American kitchens by the 1950s — today it trails only palm oil globally.

howToChoose.text: Buy plain 'vegetable oil' for value and neutrality; choose by smoke point for high heat, and keep olive or toasted oils for flavour roles instead.

storage.text: Keep sealed, cool, and dark — oil's enemy is light and heat, not time. The rulebook has the details.

foodSafetyRef.note: oil storage guidance lives in the food-safety rulebook

useItUp.text: Old oil that smells painty should go, but neutral oil never stales quickly: it greases pans, conditions cast iron, and makes simple cakes tender.
